text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PROD ALERT — Elevated 5xx + timeouts detected on inference-gateway. 5m error rate 6.7% (baseline 0.3%). P95 latency up to 3.2s. Affected routes: /v1/generate, /v1/stream. Possible source: scheduler/batching backlog. Paging @Alicia (on-call).

Alicia: Ack. I'm on call. Starting triage — opening bridge and collecting metrics. Who's got the scheduler dashboard link?

Sam: I'm pulling scheduler metrics now. Preliminary snapshot:
```
scheduler.metrics:
  queue_depth: 1187
  avg_wait_ms: 1842
  busy_workers: 42/50
  head_of_line_wait_ms: 3200
  enqueue_rate_rps: 1200
  dequeue_rate_rps: 680
```
Looks like dequeue << enqueue, consistent with saturation.

Meena: Gateway logs show a lot of 502/504s downstream when requests hit long queues. Also noticed kv-cache size spike on a few nodes.

Rob: Gateway excerpt:
```
[proxy] 2026-04-02T10:11:02Z GET /v1/generate 502 upstream_timeout host=cluster-gw-5
[proxy] 2026-04-02T10:11:06Z POST /v1/stream 504 read_timeout host=cluster-gw-2
```
This matches head-of-line stall causing callers to hit gateway timeouts.

Alicia: Triage summary — scheduler is saturated, queue growing, gateway timeouts consequential. Customer impact detected (some requests return 5xx). Immediate mitigations: 1) scale scheduler workers, 2) reduce batching parameters to lower service time per batch, 3) enable fallback routing for critical customers, 4) evict long-waiting queue items. Assigning tasks: @Meena scale, @Rob reroute / apply gateway cooldown, @Sam tweak batching.

Meena: Scaling up scheduler pool by +50% now. Running:
```bash
kubectl -n prod scale deploy/scheduler --replicas=75  # from 50 -> 75
```
I'll watch queue depth. ETA ~90s for new pods ready.

Sam: Rolling a quick batching config change to reduce max_batch_tokens and lower max_wait_ms to reduce tail latency. Pushing config via admin API:
```bash
curl -X POST https://admin.prod.redwood/api/config \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' \
  -d '{"batching": {"max_batch_tokens": 512, "max_wait_ms": 100}}'
```
Applying now. Expect shorter batches and higher throughput per second, but slightly increased compute per token.

Rob: Rerouting plan: divert 20% of traffic for /v1/generate to redwood-small-v0 (lower-latency, cheaper) as a soft-fallback to reduce pressure on main model cluster. Command:
```bash
redwood-cli rollout traffic --route=generate --model=redwood-small-v0 --pct=20
```
I'll also temporarily increase gateway read timeout to 12s to reduce 504s while backpressure clears.

Dave: Suggest evicting requests queued >2000ms to free head-of-line. Exec'ing:
```bash
curl -X POST https://admin.prod.redwood/admin/evict?older_than_ms=2000 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN'
```
This will drop timed-out calls (they'll be retried by clients or aborted). Doing it now.

Anya (CS): Noted customer impact — early telemetry shows Top impacted customers: AcmeCorp (~15% of their calls failing), Bankly (~8%), Learnify (~6%). I'm notifying account teams and prepping status updates. Please confirm ETA for stabilization so I can update customers.

IncidentBot: Bridge created — https://zoom.redwood/incident-2612345678. Incident severity: P1. Notifying execs.

Meena: New scheduler pods coming up. Queue depth trending down: 1187 -> 720 -> 410 in ~3 minutes. Dequeue rate is improving after scale.

Sam: Batching config accepted by runtime; per-node CPU up but latency tails shortened. P95 dropped from 3.2s -> 1.1s in the most loaded zone.

Rob: Started traffic rollout to redwood-small-v0. Also increased gateway read timeout to 12s. Observing fewer 504 spikes.

Alicia: After combined mitigations — scale, batching tweak, fallback routing, eviction — current metrics:
```
error_rate_5m: 1.2%
p95_latency: 890ms
queue_depth: 210
avg_wait_ms: 450
```
This is improved but still above baseline. Continuing monitoring.

Dave: Scheduling a quick hotfix to tighten scheduler backpressure thresholds and add an eviction policy for long-pending batches. I'll open a PR and aim for a canary patch to prod in the next 2 hours.

Anya: I'll send an initial customer update: brief summary + targeted mitigation + "working on durable fix". Any ETA for stable baseline?

Alicia: Expecting baseline-ish metrics within ~30-45 min if current trend continues. We'll keep bridge open. Postmortem to include root cause analysis: why dequeue << enqueue (investigate model decode path stalls, kv-cache spikes, and any recent deployments).

Meena: Noted one anomalous node with persistent high KV-cache churn; isolating it from routing to see effect.

Rob: Gateway config rollback scheduled if error rate doesn't reduce further. For now hold applied increases.

Sam: On-call handoff note: I'm taking over from Alicia at 10:35Z. Alicia — please add any context before you hand off.

Alicia: Handing off to Sam. Key things: mitigation steps applied (scale, batching change, evict, fallback), customers notified, watch the anomalous node Meena flagged. Bridge stays open. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

IncidentBot: Incident update recorded. Please add any logs/links to the incident doc.

Sam: I'll drive the next hour of monitoring and work with Dave on the hotfix canary. Will update the bridge and this thread with progress.

Anya: I'll follow up with account teams with a 30-min update.

(END OF THREAD)
